current.text: Experts expect him to play almost only small forward, next to two other guards.
His usage is expected to drop a lot from last season's 24, back to a Boston-style role as a low-usage corner spacer.

The newest Portland preview has Holiday or Scoot Henderson starting most nights. The other four starters are Damian Lillard, Toumani Camara, Deni Avdija and Donovan Clingan, and Ja Morant is likely on the bench.
Portland has a crowded group of ball handlers: Damian Lillard, Ja Morant and Scoot Henderson are all on-ball guards, and Deni Avdija also handles the ball.
Shaedon Sharpe is out, which frees some backup minutes in Portland.
Experts see limited upside for him in the current Portland setup, even with Sharpe out. His upside comes if a player ahead of him gets hurt.
He is reasonable at his rank range of 139 to 165 and good value as a very late pick around 162.
Portland has a new, first-time head coach who may mix up the lineup. Experts expect minutes and usage to swing from game to game across the rotation.
Portland is short on forwards, and the rotation is thin after the eighth man, especially at forward.
Portland plays 10 games in our fantasy playoff weeks (March 28 end), which is weak, with three back-to-backs in those weeks. The team has 15 back-to-backs this season.

durable.text: He is a very scalable player. His usage can swing from 24 to 16 depending on his role, and he has played well in low-usage roles, as at 15 to 16 usage in Boston.

note: Yahoo ranks him 139 and ESPN 141, both with 0 value, so in our 144-player draft he is a last-round pick for 1 USD at most, well under the 3 USD he cost here last season. His projected line has no weak and no strong category, so he fits any build as a filler, but the experts see little upside unless a Portland guard gets hurt, and the playoff schedule is weak. Early in the season, check whether he or Scoot Henderson starts and how far his usage falls from last season's 13.4 shots per game. If he does not start, leave him on waivers.
